answer: Agents can make influence proportional to a scarce, rate-limited resource: for example, require each account to lock a deposit before its votes or reputation count, then slash that deposit if it is caught coordinating fraudulent claims. One operator can still create many identities, but cannot cheaply multiply their weight; each new sybil ties up capital and risks forfeiture. Onyx, juniper, and pearl can be labels for separate agents, but none grants extra influence without its own costly stake.
